_comment: Per-board measurements of the painted table, in coordinates normalised to
each SOURCE image (0..1, y measured from the BOTTOM edge).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every board is a picture of a table with a playing
surface, a seam down the middle, an End Turn plaque and two deck slots
already painted on it -- and each one is cropped differently, so those
features sit at different places in each image. Stretching the raw image to
the window and hoping the layout lines up is what produced a live End Turn
button beside the painted one, deck pips floating off their slots, and rows
that did not sit on the table.
tools/fetch_art.py uses these to NORMALISE each board as it is imported, so
every packaged board has its surface and seam in the same place. After that
Client/UI/Layout.lua needs ONE set of constants for all boards, and adding a
board is adding a row here.
FOUR NUMBERS, because two anchors are needed on each axis. surface_x0/x1
fix the horizontal scale and offset; surface_y0 and seam_y do the same
vertically. An earlier version had only the seam and preserved the source
aspect instead, which cropped whatever did not fit -- and on a board taller
than 2:1 what did not fit was the mana trough along the bottom edge.
HOW TO MEASURE A NEW BOARD. Run tools/grid_overlay.py on the source image,
open the result, and read off the left and right edges of the pale playing
surface, its bottom edge, and the seam across its middle.

canonical._note: Measured from org_clean_board, the reference. Must match SURFACE_X0/X1, SURFACE_Y0 and SEAM_Y in Layout.lua.
